free_tier.stated: No published byte quota, no published per-file cap, and no paid storage tier exists to upsell to — the only paid Ollama product is inference compute ('Pricing': Free $0 'Use any cloud model with pay-as-you-go usage credits', Pro $20/mo; nothing on that page meters model storage). A single repo holds 455.5 GiB in one layer.

per_object_cap.stated: per-object-cap: NOT published, and NOT 2 GiB

retention.stated: client-side chunking is 100 MB-1 GB parts (server/upload.go). Retention: none — objects persist until deleted; no TTL anywhere in the docs

egress.terms: Unmetered anonymous pull. No egress line exists anywhere in Ollama's pricing — there is no per-GB transfer meter to quote because pull is free and unauthenticated. Blob GET is 307 to an R2 bucket (dd20bb891979d25aebc8bec07b2b3bbc.r2.cloudflarestorage.com, X-Amz-Expires=86400), fronted by Cloudflare.

tooling: Native OCI Distribution v2. `ollama push` / `ollama pull`, oras/skopeo/crane all work. Push requires a free ollama.com account (WorkOS authkit signup, no payment); pull is fully anonymous. `ollama create` accepts safetensors dirs, GGUF, split GGUF globs, and any layer content — a pushed model is just OCI layers, so arbitrary bytes ride as `application/vnd.ollama.image.model`.
chaining: unlimited free namespaces x unlimited repos x unlimited tags; the binding per-object ceiling is whatever the server accepts, and 455 GiB single-blob objects already exist in production. 30 TiB = 66 objects the size of huihui_ai/kimi-k2-abliterated. Multiply by free-account count. This is structurally identical to GHCR but with a ~45x larger observed per-object ceiling and no documented 10 GB layer cap.

limits_note: per-object-cap: NOT published, and NOT 2 GiB like GitHub — verified live at 489,088,538,784 bytes in one blob. Retention: none — objects persist until deleted; no TTL anywhere in the docs. request-rate: not published; 20 consecutive ranged GETs all returned 206 with no throttling.
reliability_note: Pushes to large blobs are flaky: issue #6466 reports 502 Bad Gateway at 40-50% of an 8.5 GB upload, and #13740 reports 413 on 100 GB — resume/retry is required, and `ollama push` is not resumable by default. Reads were 100% stable in every probe.
